en.title: Agreement with the noun
en.summary: English adjectives never change to agree with the noun they describe.

paragraphs: In many languages an adjective changes its ending to match the noun in gender and number. English does not do this. The same adjective is used with a singular noun, a plural noun, a male person and a female person.

English adjectives are invariable: the form never changes. Only the noun changes, and only for number. The demonstratives this and that are the exception, because they take the plural forms these and those.

blocks.html:
SingularPlural
a new carnew cars
a tall womantall women
this red applethese red apples
that old housethose old houses
a happy childhappy children

paragraphs: Some words that come before the noun do agree in number. We say one book but many books, and this book but these books. The adjective itself, such as new, stays the same.
If your own language has gender and plural endings on adjectives, English is easier here. There is nothing to add. The difficulty is only to remember not to add anything.

items: Wrong: **two bigs dogs** Right: **two big dogs**
Wrong: **a beautifuls girl** Right: **a beautiful girl**
Wrong: **these book** Right: **this book** or **these books**

ro.title: Acordul cu substantivul
ro.summary: În limba română, adjectivul își schimbă forma după genul și numărul substantivului pe care îl descrie.

paragraphs: Adjectivul este un cuvânt care descrie un substantiv. În limba română, adjectivul se acordă mereu cu substantivul. El își schimbă terminația după gen și număr.
Adjectivul se așază de obicei după substantiv. Forma lui se schimbă la masculin, feminin și neutru. La plural, terminația adjectivului se schimbă din nou.
